transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-03-21
Start Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (AlphaHealth PM), Dr. Kevin Morales (AlphaHealth Head of AI), James Lee (AlphaHealth Platform Eng)

Summary:
Redwood and AlphaHealth scoped a POC focused on integrating Redwood's hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints for clinical note summarization and structured extraction. Discussed success criteria (latency, accuracy, hallucination thresholds), workload sizing (qps, token lengths), benchmark plan, timelines, and integration options (SDKs vs raw REST, function/tool calling for structured JSON output). Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Success criteria and evaluation metrics
- Workload sizing and peak traffic
- Benchmark plan and sample dataset
- Integration approach: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Function/tool calling and structured output schemas
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC 2

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intro then jump into the POC scope. Maya from Redwood here, with Liam from our SE team.
[00:00:10] Sara Patel: Hi Maya, thanks, Sara here. We're excited to see how Redwood can help with our clinical summarization flows.
[00:00:15] Liam O'Connor: Hey Sara, Kevin, James, good to meet you. Just to set expectations, we usually run a benchmark with real-ish payloads, measure p50/p95 latency, token cost, and then iterate on batching/quant profiles.
[00:00:28] Dr. Kevin Morales: Great. Our primary goal is to automate outpatient note summarization and extract structured problem lists. Key success criteria are accuracy vs our human baseline, hallucination under 2% for critical fields, and p95 latency under 400ms for single-record calls.
[00:00:45] James Lee: To add, we need compatibility with our existing API gateway. Prefer OpenAI-compatible endpoints so minimal client changes. Also need the ability to call functions or tools to return strict JSON schema for downstream pipelines.
[00:00:58] Maya Chen: Yep that's doable. We support OpenAI-compatible REST and our SDKs (Node, Python, Go). For function/tool calling we support the common function calling pattern and can enforce structured output via schema guidance and post-validators.
[00:01:14] Sara Patel: Quick question on token sizes — our typical encounter is 1.5k tokens after concatenating notes and metadata, occasionally up to 4k. Can you run benchmarks at those sizes?
[00:01:26] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely, we'll parameterize by seq len. For 1.5k we expect lower latency; 4k will be heavier but we can show cost/latency tradeoffs and suggest quantization or chunking strategies.
[00:01:38] Dr. Kevin Morales: Also confidentiality — can we run the POC in a private VPC? We need audit logs and KMS integration for keys.
[00:01:46] Maya Chen: For POCs we normally run on our hosted environment but we can provision a private VPC-enabled instance for AlphaHealth's POC. We'll include KMS options and audit log access; security docs will be shared.
[00:01:59] James Lee: That's good. What about throughput — we expect ~40 rps during peak sync windows and avg 10 rps otherwise. Also some batch jobs that process 200 notes per minute.
[00:02:11] Liam O'Connor: 40 rps of 1.5k tokens is a meaningful baseline. We'll model continuous batching vs single-request latency. For background batch jobs, we can recommend batching to 200 note chunks to optimize throughput and cost.
[00:02:25] Sara Patel: For success criteria, besides hallucination and latency, we'll measure structured extraction F1 > 0.88 and end-to-end processing cost under $0.03 per note. We can be flexible on cost but want to understand unit economics.
[00:02:40] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include per-note cost estimates in the benchmark report. We'll also run accuracy evals against your labeled set and produce confusion matrices.
[00:02:50] Dr. Kevin Morales: On integration, our devs prefer using the OpenAI-compatible SDK to minimize refactor. Do Redwood SDKs mirror OpenAI SDKs? Any function-calling differences?
[00:03:02] Liam O'Connor: Our SDKs intentionally mimic OpenAI patterns: create/chat/completions, call functions with defined schemas. There are small differences in streaming tokens and error codes but we'll document them. If you want, we can provide a compatibility shim.
[00:03:18] Sara Patel: Would be great if we could just swap endpoint URLs and keep the same client code.
[00:03:22] Maya Chen: That's the goal. We'll provide example snippets for Python/Node showing minimal changes. Also we'll include guidance for structured output: use our function calling with a JSON schema and then a secondary layer to enforce strict typing.
[00:03:35] James Lee: About tool calling — we want the model to call our lookup service for drug interactions. Can Redwood route those calls back to our internal tool endpoint securely?
[00:03:47] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support tool/function calling where the runtime can emit a tool call event that your backend can receive via webhook inside the VPC, or we can connect via a private peering. We can sign callbacks and provide retries.
[00:03:59] Dr. Kevin Morales: How do you prevent leakage of PHI to logs or model retraining?
[00:04:05] Maya Chen: We have options: disable training data persistence for your tenant, redact sensitive fields pre-send with client-side rules, and KMS-backed encryption for logs. We'll include the Data Processing addendum in the security pack.
[00:04:18] Sara Patel: Great. Timeline wise, we'd like a 4-week POC: week 1 ingestion & baseline, week 2 benchmarks, week 3 integration/dev, week 4 evaluation & decision. Is that realistic?
[00:04:30] Liam O'Connor: Yes that's fairly standard. We'll plan the benchmark within the first 10 days and share results within 48 hours of run. Integration work can run in parallel once we provide SDKs and sample snippets.
[00:04:42] James Lee: For the benchmark, we'll provide a 2k-record sample set with varied token lengths and labels. We'll need you to run both hosted and a private VPC run to compare.
[00:04:54] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll run both if you can provide network access for the VPC test or a mocked dataset. We'll also include a Dedicated capacity pricing option in the proposal.
[00:05:06] Sara Patel: For acceptance criteria, we'll use: F1 >= 0.88 on extraction tasks, hallucination < 2%, p95 latency < 400ms for single calls, and cost projection under $0.03 per note.
[00:05:18] Dr. Kevin Morales: And we'll include security checklist items — SOC2, ability to rotate keys, SSO/SAML for Redwood Console access.
[00:05:26] Liam O'Connor: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and we can rotate keys via KMS. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[00:05:34] Sara Patel: Ok specifics on SDKs — can you share code examples for sending a function call with our schema and receiving structured JSON back?
[00:05:41] Maya Chen: Yes we'll share a repo snippet. Example flow: create chat with system prompt, include function schema for problem_list extraction, call createChatCompletion with function_calls enabled, then parse the returned JSON. We'll also show how to stream partials for UI.
[00:05:55] James Lee: Do you support OpenAPI spec generated tool schemas or do we need to hand craft the JSON schema?
[00:06:02] Liam O'Connor: We can accept OpenAPI-style definitions and convert them; we recommend JSON Schema for function calling. We have a small utility to convert common OpenAPI fields.
[00:06:14] Dr. Kevin Morales: On monitoring, we'll need per-token cost breakdown, latency by route, and error rates. Is that in Redwood Console?
[00:06:22] Maya Chen: Yes Console provides per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, and traces. We'll give you read-only access to a demo console and then provision tenant access during POC.
[00:06:33] Sara Patel: Any limitations around streaming for function-calling? We want to show progressive extraction in the UI.
[00:06:40] Liam O'Connor: Streaming supports partial tokens but function-calls are emitted as final structured payloads; we can stream intermediate content and then emit the function object as a final event.
[00:06:52] James Lee: For regression testing, can we run evals automatically on pushes? Hook into CI?
[00:06:58] Maya Chen: Yes Redwood Optimize supports automated eval runs and regression alerts tied to your prompt sets. We can integrate with CI to trigger evals post-deploy.
[00:07:08] Dr. Kevin Morales: Who will be our points of contact during POC?
[00:07:12] Maya Chen: Primary AE is me, technical lead is Liam. We'll also loop in a solutions engineer and security lead if needed.
[00:07:18] Sara Patel: Ok let's recap next steps.
[00:07:20] Maya Chen: Action items: James to upload sample dataset to secure link; Maya to kick off benchmark; Liam to prepare function-calling demo; Redwood to send security pack and sample SDK snippets.
[00:07:34] Sara Patel: Timeline — aim to start benchmark by 2025-03-24 and have first results by 2025-03-26.
[00:07:41] Maya Chen: We'll aim for that. Any other questions?
[00:07:45] Dr. Kevin Morales: One last — what about fallback model behavior if the primary model is overloaded?
[00:07:51] Liam O'Connor: We have smart routing and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants; we can configure a cost-performance fallback policy so you retain availability.
[00:07:59] James Lee: Good. Also please include a sample OpenAI-compatible endpoint URL and minimal curl examples.
[00:08:05] Maya Chen: We'll include those in the SDK pack. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the benchmark schedule and docs.
[00:08:13] Sara Patel: Thanks, bye.

Notes (occasional transcription artifacts): 'K-V cache' mentioned (should be KV cache), 'SAML' clearly stated, minor filler words and overlapping speech in places. Some proper nouns may be slightly off in the automated transcript.

End of meeting.
